source_batch.unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U24: Classify mortgage forms by possession,covenant and transfer terms

payload.title: Classify from legal features,not the product name
payload.core_explanation_md:
A simple mortgage combines the described personal repayment covenant and right to cause sale without delivering possession. A usufructuary mortgage centres on possession and appropriation of rents/profits under its terms. An English mortgage has the specified repayment date and absolute transfer subject to retransfer. A conditional-sale mortgage needs the statutory condition in the same instrument effecting the ostensible sale. An anomalous mortgage is the residual statutory category.

For deposit of title deeds,the debt,delivery and security intention matter,together with the prescribed place of deposit. The property itself need not be located in that notified town. A memorandum that creates the bargain and one merely recording a completed deposit require different registration analysis,with State stamping/registration amendments checked separately.

self_check.prompt_text: Is the property location necessarily the same as the required place of title-deed deposit?

payload.stem_md: Deeds are held for safekeeping with no security intention established. Can the bank infer a mortgage merely from custody?

options.text_md: No; the security intention and other requirements must be established
Yes,all safe custody creates a mortgage
Yes,if the envelope is labelled original
options.explanation_md: The label does not establish the bargain.

options.text_md: No deposit-of-deeds mortgage can ever exist

payload.stem_md: An ostensible sale relies on a mortgage condition contained only in a separate document. Which statutory feature needs attention?

options.text_md: A rule that possession determines every mortgage type
The same-document condition for the described conditional-sale mortgage
options.explanation_md: The location of the condition is material.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The location of the condition is material.
